proposal.utterance: How should 'sustaining practice' (the practice that sustains an institution over time) be classified in BFO?

entities.label: SustainingPractice
entities.rationale: A sustaining practice is a temporally extended happening — a pattern of repeated behavior (e.g., officials applying rules, citizens obeying norms, courts enforcing statutes) that unfolds in time and causally maintains an institution. This maps naturally to BFO Process (BFO_0000015): it has temporal parts, it occurs, and it is not merely a disposition or quality. It is distinct from BehavioralLegalManifestation (which covers individual behavioral expressions of legal norms) in that SustainingPractice emphasizes the aggregate, recurrent process that keeps an institution in existence over time. No existing working class captures this composite sustaining function precisely enough to reuse.

relations.rationale: SustainingPractice is a subclass of Process: instances are temporally extended occurrents that unfold through time and sustain an institution.

Candidate sub-typing: SustainingPractice may be understood as a species of BehavioralLegalManifestation — the behavioral-process side — specifically the aggregate, institution-sustaining form. This is flagged as a candidate and placed in open_questions because the user may prefer to keep SustainingPractice as a sibling rather than a subclass if the two are meant to carve different phenomena.

Instances of SustainingPractice have as participant the LegalInstitution they sustain (process has_participant material entity), capturing the dependence of institutional persistence on the sustaining process.

InstitutionalPersistence (a Quality, BFO_0000019, already in the ontology) is realized in — or more precisely, its bearer's persistence is grounded in — SustainingPractice. Strictly BFO_0000054 (realized in) applies to Realizable entities; InstitutionalPersistence is typed as Quality. This relation is therefore a candidate and flagged in open_questions: we may need to recast InstitutionalPersistence as a Disposition to make realized_in well-typed.

open_questions: Should SustainingPractice be a subclass of BehavioralLegalManifestation, or a sibling under BFO Process? The distinction turns on whether individual behavioral acts and aggregate sustaining practices are meant to be the same phenomenon at different granularities.

Should InstitutionalPersistence be retyped from Quality (BFO_0000019) to Disposition (BFO_0000016) so that 'realized in SustainingPractice' is well-typed under BFO? A disposition is internally grounded and realized in a process; a quality is not realizable in the BFO sense.

Is SustainingPractice intended to cover only official practices (e.g., judges deciding cases), or also citizen-level practices (e.g., general compliance)? This may motivate subclassing into OfficialSustainingPractice and PopularSustainingPractice.

Should SustainingPractice have temporal parts corresponding to specific episodes, or is it modeled as a single maximally continuous process? This affects whether BFO_0000050 (part of) relations to temporal intervals are needed.
proposal.rationale_summary: The concept of 'sustaining practice' — the ongoing social activity that keeps a legal institution in existence over time — is best classified as a BFO Process (BFO_0000015). Processes are occurrents that unfold in time, have temporal parts, and can have participants; a sustaining practice paradigmatically involves repeated actions by officials and subjects that collectively maintain an institution. It is not a Quality (which inheres in a bearer at a time without itself unfolding), not a Disposition (which is an internally grounded capacity, not an activity), and not a Generically Dependent Continuant (which is an information artifact). The new class SustainingPractice is introduced as a subclass of BFO_0000015 and is linked to LegalInstitution via has_participant and to InstitutionalPersistence via a candidate realized_in relation (flagged for review because InstitutionalPersistence is currently typed as Quality rather than Disposition). A possible subclass relation to BehavioralLegalManifestation is proposed but queued as an open question because the two classes may be intended to carve distinct levels of description.
